CAP.counters.cap.clamp: Gate(name='cap.clamp', fired=False, value='0 clamped of 0 lift(s) taken', threshold='0 clamped -- every earned lift applied in full', reachable=False, reason="NO LIFT CAN BE HELD AT A HARD CEILING on this configuration, which is the only event this gate counts. A clamp needs three things IN ORDER -- a lift EARNED, that lift APPLIED rather than refused, and its unclamped arithmetic ABOVE the hard ceiling -- and on every arm here one of the three fails first: (expert) NOT ARMED, so NO LIFT IS EVER EARNED on it: CAP_TARGETS=off does not arm this arm, and a clamp is a property of a lift; (vocabulary) NOT ARMED, so NO LIFT IS EVER EARNED on it: CAP_TARGETS=off does not arm this arm, and a clamp is a property of a lift. THE VERDICT ABOVE IS NOT A CLAIM THAT NO LIFT IS EARNED and must not be read as one -- the clauses above say, per arm, which case it is in: an arm's earned lifts can be refused by name, and an applied lift can move nothing, and either of those reaches this verdict with lifts having been earned all along. What became of an EARNED lift is cap.valve's line and the block-reason histogram's number; what became of an APPLIED one that overshot is this line's, and there are none here. Reported unreachable rather than as 0 clamped lifts, which would read as a valve that lifted freely and was never held -- the same confusion between an inert mechanism and an absent one that cap.valve is unreachable here to avoid.")
